note: The desk's forward calendar (audit items 2 and 5). ONE file, read every run: week_ahead.py renders Monday's Week Ahead story from it, and calendar_check.py flags any event the desk has NOT covered so the editor sees the gap instead of missing it (the Zcash Ironwood upgrade of 2026-07-28 is exactly the case that motivated this). Only scheduled, publicly announced items belong here, each with a source URL. Nothing here may be a prediction: kinds are macro, earnings, protocol, regulatory. 'match' is a list of AND-groups: the event counts as covered when one story contains every term of any one group. Never use a bare entity name as a group on its own, or an unrelated old story about that entity will claim coverage the desk never gave.

events.title: Zcash activates the Ironwood upgrade (NU6.3)
events.detail: Zcash's Ironwood network upgrade activates at block height 3,428,143, replacing the Orchard shielded pool after a counterfeiting bug was disclosed. Funds leaving Orchard must pass a supply-accounting checkpoint, and the network runs Zebra-only after the end-of-support halt that preceded activation.

events.title: FOMC rate decision
events.detail: The Federal Open Market Committee meets Tuesday and Wednesday; the rate decision lands Wednesday at 2:00 p.m. Eastern with a press conference at 2:30. This meeting carries no Summary of Economic Projections, so there is no dot plot to parse.

events.title: Coinbase second-quarter results
events.detail: Coinbase reports second-quarter results after the U.S. market close, the largest listed crypto exchange's first report since the June market drawdown.

events.title: Strategy second-quarter results
events.detail: Strategy, the largest corporate bitcoin holder, reports second-quarter results after the close with a webinar at 5:00 p.m. Eastern; its bitcoin position marks to the quarter's prices.
events.note: Match terms deliberately avoid bare 'strategy': the company name is a common noun and body prose matched it against the Coinbase earnings story (2026-08-02). Ticker and founder are distinctive; the calendar's own rule against bare entity names applies double to entities named after common nouns.
